completed_work.summary: Stage 1 architecture phase. Read the entire legacy codebase. Moved every pre-existing file into _legacy/ preserving internal structure (nothing deleted). Wrote ARCHITECTURE.md (full new design: stage boundaries, state machine, all handoff contracts, bot UX, modes, preserved-subsystem integration), BUILD_PROGRESS.json (this file), NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md (reusable handoff prompt with credential placeholders), fresh README.md and .gitignore at root.

Built the contracts_and_schemas phase — every downstream phase now has a stable foundation to import. (1) Four JSON Schemas at schemas/: job_status.schema.json, stage_a_request.schema.json, production_plan.schema.json, analysis_bundle.schema.json — all four validated as well-formed Draft 2020-12. (2) pipeline/plan/schema.py — the single Python production.json validator (ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3 rules). (3) bot/src/plan.js — the JS port. Both accept the ARCHITECTURE.md nested `series` object AND the legacy flat `series_*` siblings, and both accept `voiceover_text` OR legacy `raw_narration`. (4) pipeline/status.py — atomic status.json writer + ten-state state machine (ARCHITECTURE.md §6). Refuses to leave terminal states (complete/error/cancelled) except into another terminal state. CLI entry point for GitHub Actions. (5) bot/src/jobs.js — pure JS state-machine helpers (newStatus / mergeStatus / canTransition / serializeStatus / statusPath) that share constants with the Python side. (6) Tests: pipeline/tests/test_status.py (13 cases), pipeline/tests/test_plan_cross_validation.py (2 cases including the JS/Python equivalence check driven by a 26-document language-neutral fixture at pipeline/tests/fixtures/plan_cases.json via a Node shim at pipeline/tests/run_js_validator.mjs), bot/test/plan.test.mjs + bot/test/jobs.test.mjs (15 JS cases). All 15 Python tests and 15 JS tests pass locally; the Python↔JS cross-language equivalence check passes on every fixture. Recorded one architecture_concern (nested-vs-flat series shape) — resolved for now by accepting both, but the operator should decide the canonical form before Automatic mode is built.

architecture_concerns.decision_at_stake: ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3 documents production.json's series data as a NESTED object (`series.series_id`, `series.part`, `series.start_seconds`, `series.end_seconds`, `series.is_final`, `series.summary`). The legacy contract (_legacy/schemas/production_plan_contract.json and _legacy/scripts/production_plan_contract.py) uses FLAT sibling fields (`series_id`, `series_part`, `series_start_seconds`, `series_end_seconds`, `series_final`, `series_summary`). ARCHITECTURE.md §14 also states 'the production.json field names and validation semantics' are intentionally NOT changing — which is in tension with the nested rewrite in §7.3. Existing legacy plans, and the legacy manual browser tool that users still paste output from, all use the flat shape.
architecture_concerns.why_i_think_this_needs_attention: Two producers (external agents pasted by the user in Manual mode, and any tool referencing the old browser validator) will keep emitting the flat shape. If Stage B were coded to accept only the nested shape it would reject every legacy plan on sight; if the flat shape were coded to be the only accepted shape, we would drift from ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3. Only the operator can decide which is canonical.
architecture_concerns.what_i_did_for_now: Applied the closest-analog policy: accepted BOTH shapes in schema.py and plan.js (nested wins per-field when both are present), mirroring the already-established precedent of accepting `raw_narration` alongside `voiceover_text`. Continued to build against ARCHITECTURE.md as written — the nested shape is preferred and documented as such. This does not silently redesign anything: both shapes validate to identical semantics.
architecture_concerns.what_the_right_answer_probably_is: Pick one. If Stage B ports cleanly from the legacy scripts (which read `series_id`, `series_part`, …), the FLAT shape is the pragmatic canonical and ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3 should be revised to match. If the nested shape is genuinely preferred, add a note in §7.3 that legacy flat form is accepted for input but is deprecated on output — and update 00_READ_THIS_FIRST.txt (the analysis prompt) so external agents emit the nested shape.
architecture_concerns.action_requested: Operator: pick a canonical shape and update ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3 / §14 accordingly. Until then future sessions should keep accepting both — do NOT delete either code path in schema.py or plan.js without operator sign-off.

last_session.final_note: contracts_and_schemas is complete and pushed. Every later phase can now `from pipeline.plan.schema import validate_production_plan`, `from pipeline import status`, `import { validateProductionPlan } from '../src/plan.js'`, and `import { newStatus, mergeStatus, canTransition } from '../src/jobs.js'`. The cross-language equivalence test guarantees the two validators stay honest — a change to one that isn't mirrored in the other will fail CI as soon as the test is added to a workflow. Next session starts stage_b_render.
